correctness.rationale: The diffeomorphism q=-log(1-y) gives qdot=x and potential U_c(q)=(1-c)q+(1-2c)(exp(-q)-1)+(c/2)(exp(-2q)-1), Uc derivative=(1-exp(-q))*(1-c*(1-exp(-q))). Left side q<0 is strictly restoring and tends to infinity for h>=0. Right potential increases without bound for k<1, tends to 1/2 for k=1, and has a unique maximum at q_s=log(k/(k-1)) with barrier E*=1-1/(2k)+(k-1)log(1-1/k), curvature -(k-1)/k, for k>1. Period quadrature sqrt(2)*integral dq/sqrt(E-V(q)) gives linear-tail sqrt(E), exactly integrated critical potential gives inverse-square-root and the outgoing qdot gives t^2(1-y)->2 and t*x->2, and nondegenerate saddle curvature gives the logarithmic coefficient 1/sqrt((k-1)/k). The left contribution is lower order/bounded in all edge limits, so leading terms do not depend on h. Independently checked numerical potential derivatives for multiple h,k and exact saddle height; finite checks do not prove edge asymptotics. No period monotonicity claimed.

value.rationale: The explicit global transition between an unbounded linear potential, a limiting finite-height barrier at infinity, and a finite saddle is a natural complete classification in a motivated quadratic center family. Exact three different physical-time period exponents, escape coefficients and independence from the lower-zone parameter provide sharp dynamical boundary information beyond textbook local center tests.

final_claim: For xdot=-y+c(y)y^2, ydot=x(1-y), c=k for y>=0 and h for y<0 with h,k>=0 on y<1, the maximal origin period annulus changes at k=1: global for k<1 with T~2sqrt(2E)/(1-k), infinite-position energy edge E=1/2 for k=1 with T~pi sqrt(2)/sqrt(1/2-E) and exact escape scaling, and saddle loop at E*(k)>0 for k>1 with T=sqrt(k/(k-1))*log(1/(E*-E))+O(1), independent leading coefficients from h.
limitations: Only nonnegative h,k and invariant half-plane y<1; no classification of unrelated quadratic families.
